findings.title: Null dereference when no destination calendar and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar, which `handleNewBooking` produces as `null`. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Any Google Meet booking for a user without a destination calendar therefore throws a TypeError and fails the booking. Before this change the code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and fell back to Cal Video. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Inverted slug condition in organization creation
findings.body: The original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set the slug only when team billing is disabled. The new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` reverses that. With billing enabled, orgs now get their slug immediately, bypassing the payment/requestedSlug flow. Self-hosted instances without billing now create orgs with no slug at all. This change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and looks like an accidental logic flip.

findings.title: Collective hosts' calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. Every other collective host's destination calendar is silently discarded and they receive no calendar event, which is the exact bug this PR is meant to fix. Initialize to an array, e.g. `[...main, ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: Hangout patch uses possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` when no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert call falls back with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. With `undefined` that request fails, so the Meet link is never written into the event description. Use the same `|| "primary"` fallback in the patch.

findings.title: Dead fallback in calendar id resolution for update/delete
findings.body: The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches for a calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId`, which can never match a real calendar, so `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined` in that path. Previously it fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. In `updateEvent`, `undefined` is passed as `calendarId` and the Google API call fails. The same pattern is in `deleteEvent` (line 317). Fall back to the first or credential-matching destination calendar instead.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use main host's calendar id
findings.body: `createEvent` is now called once per destination calendar with each host's own credential. Office365 ignores the credentialId and always uses `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, the main host's calendar. For a second collective host on Outlook, the request targets `/me/calendars/<other user's id>/events` and fails. Lark (`createEvent`/`createAttendees`) and CalDAV `BaseCalendarService` have the same problem. Only Google selects the calendar by credentialId, so multi-host support is broken for every other provider.

findings.title: Undefined credential passed to updateEvent; rejection escapes try/catch
findings.body: If the credential is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor found in the DB (deleted, or no app slug), `credential` is still `undefined` when `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is called. `updateEvent` reads `credential.appName`, so the async call rejects. The function then does `return Promise.all(result)` without `await` inside the `try`. That rejection bypasses the catch block that is supposed to turn failures into `success: false` results, so the whole reschedule or location update throws. Skip references with no credential and `await` the `Promise.all`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation logic repeated per reference and only deletes first reference
findings.body: The recurring-series delete block now sits inside the loop over calendar references. For N references it re-runs N times over all of the organizer's calendar credentials. Each pass deletes only the first `_calendar` reference of each updated booking (`references.find`). Other hosts' calendar events for the recurring series are never deleted, and the main host's events get duplicate delete attempts.

findings.title: loadUsers dropped organization select for dynamic users
findings.body: The rewrite of `loadUsers` removed `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-group user query. Downstream code that relies on `user.organization` gets `undefined` for dynamic group bookings, e.g. when building org-aware booker URLs. The rewrite also turns validation failures (an empty `dynamicUserList`) into generic 500 errors.
